sections.markdown:
## D — Accuracy notes and source flags: general driving: school bus exceptions, parking, lane changes, highway entry and exit, passing and the zipper merge
Every C and C2 fact cites exactly one physical manual page from the selected range; nothing relies on outside knowledge.
Physical page 84 says you may move on once the bus moves or its red lights stop flashing, while page 82 in the previous section says to proceed after the red and/or amber lights stop and the stop arm is no longer visible; both are reported as printed and the difference is held as typed debt [A01].
The hill parking caption on page 88 prints downhill with or without a curve, which reads as curb; part C teaches the downhill rule from the page 87 text and cites the caption only for its summary [A05].
Page 88 describes blind spots as areas around your vehicle that other vehicles cannot see, unlike the earlier definition of areas where your own view is blocked; the dossier does not reuse the page 88 wording [A05].
Page 89 says to move early to the lane closest to your existing point, read here as your exit point [A06].
The zipper merge backup reduction of up to forty percent is the manual's own figure with no cited study, so it is reported as the manual's claim [A08].

corpus_stability.reason: The South Carolina Driver's Manual prints a single edition line (Revised 06/2024) on its front cover; its disclaimer says legislative and SCDMV policy changes may make some content out of date until the agency incorporates them, and a possibly newer unlinked upload exists on the issuer site (freshness debt in the run jams), so the corpus is treated as revised at most about once a year, bound to the registered snapshot.

verification_debt.claim_text: Physical page 84 (citing SC Code §56-5-2760) says not to proceed until the school bus moves or its red lights stop flashing, while page 82 says to proceed slowly after the red and/or amber lights stop flashing and the stop arm is no longer visible; the statute text was not read to reconcile the two.
